timeline.event: A Pakistani Taliban suicide bomber drove an explosive-laden vehicle into a Pakistan Armed Forces convoy before detonating the explosives
The explosives detonated, killing the bomber and 13 soldiers
29 people were injured, including six children and women
The explosion caused the roofs of two houses to collapse, injuring six children
The explosion caused damage to other nearby houses
The death toll was later confirmed to have reached 13 while the number of injuries increased to 29, including 19 civilians
An initial probe found that approximately 800 kilograms (1,760 pounds) of explosives were used in the bombing
In response to the attack, 14 militants were killed in subsequent operations
The Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) later claimed that the Pakistani Taliban and India were linked to the bombing
President Asif Ali Zardari condemned the attack and paid tribute to the victims
The army chief of staff, Field Marshal Asim Munir, said in a statement that any actions to undermine Pakistan's internal stability would be met with decisive retribution
Ali Amin Gandapur, the chief minister of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, condemned the attack
The Hafiz Gul Bahadur Group, an armed faction of the Pakistani Taliban, claimed responsibility for the attack
Footage of the explosion showed bandaged children lying on the floor near shattered glass and debris
The vehicle hit a military truck full of soldiers responsible for disposing bombs and other explosives

plan.question: How did an explosives-laden vehicle strike a bomb disposal unit with devastating force?

chapters.title: A Sudden Shockwave
beats: A devastating blast rips through a military convoy along a transit route, instantly leveling nearby domestic structures.
The catastrophic explosion claims the lives of thirteen soldiers tasked with defusing ordnance and leaves twenty-nine people wounded.
The blast shatters an entire neighborhood, demonstrating how a single catastrophic breach can devastate highly trained defense units and nearby civilian lives.

chapters.title: The Convoy and the Commanders
beats: A specialized military truck travels as part of a Pakistan Armed Forces convoy, manned by soldiers trained specifically to dispose of bombs and volatile munitions.
Field Marshal Asim Munir, as Army Chief of Staff, oversees operational readiness and demands internal stability against persistent armed insurgencies.
President Asif Ali Zardari maintains executive responsibility over national security while armed factions continue to test state authority in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

chapters.title: The Intercept Path
beats: An insurgent driver navigates an explosive-laden vehicle into the path of the approaching military convoy.
The vehicle closes the distance toward the military truck carrying the specialized ordnance disposal team.
The convoy moves through a populated corridor where residential roofs sit directly adjacent to the roadway.

chapters.title: The Ramming
beats: A Pakistani Taliban suicide bomber steers the explosive-laden vehicle directly into the Pakistan Armed Forces convoy.
The vehicle slams directly into the military truck carrying the soldiers responsible for disposing bombs.

chapters.title: Eight Hundred Kilograms
beats: The suicide bomber detonates roughly 800 kilograms of explosives, killing the bomber and thirteen soldiers instantly.
The shockwave tears outward, causing the roofs of two nearby houses to collapse and damaging multiple surrounding homes.

chapters.title: The Retribution and Fallout
beats: The Hafiz Gul Bahadur Group, an armed faction of the Pakistani Taliban, claims responsibility for the attack.
President Asif Ali Zardari condemns the attack and pays tribute to the victims, while Field Marshal Asim Munir vows that any actions to undermine stability will meet decisive retribution.
